title: The rule-contract C row, the ordering column, the version label, the record consumer list and two consumed operation names are unsettled for the payment-matching slice, and the legacy AC6 load is not this story's
source: Work Package B2-P8-002 story line RWB-P8-E2027-APP; Template and Rules v1 R5.4, R5.5 DP-04 and R7.2 s12; RWB-E2-027 sections 3, 7, 10, 11 and 12; FSD P8 v3 A2.1.4.3 (AC-EXC-P8-001-07); TSD P8 v2 T3.1 (DF-REF-270), T5.3 and T-A.2; RWB-P3-E2042 precondition (version label PMT-2026.12); Arch v5 slides 42, 43 and 44 through the P8 context pack
description: Five defects sit in one slice and are carried as one combined row. (1) Dependency: legacy AC6 loads the package version through POST /api/recovery/v1/admin/rule-packages/PAYMENT_MATCH/versions, whose checks belong to the registry of rwb-decision, and DP-04 adds C RWB-P7-E1073-CON, but the metadata C row of this key carries only the three rwb-case contracts. (2) Naming: the story, its Background and this slice call the ordering of the PAYMENT_MATCH rows row order, while TSD P8 v2 T3.1 names the column priority (DF-REF-270) and FSD AC-EXC-P8-001-07 says priority 2 for the same invalid version. (3) Rule label: RWB-E2-027 puts version PM-2026.12 in force from 2026-12-01 while the rwb-case story of the same package code uses PMT-2026.12 from 2026-12-15, so two labels for one package would leave two versions in force. (4) Events: Arch v5 slide 42 row 08 lists rwb-decision and rwb-reporting as the consumers of DecisionRecorded, while the service conventions of this key list it as consumed here. (5) Contract: the rule-evaluation result has no published schema, no row-order field and no operation name for the version-in-force read, and the treatment installment-paid operation has no name, so the consumed surface of this slice carries the placeholder. The legacy AC6 When step is also written on the monolith base and not on /api/recovery/decision/v1.
evidence: Work Package B2-P8-002 story line (service rwb-payment, patterns DP04 with C row RWB-P3-E1042-CON, RWB-P3-E1043-CON and RWB-P3-E2042-CON only, acs AC6, AC7 and AC10, H row without RWB-P7-E1073-CON); RWB-E2-027 section 7 AC6 When step and section 12 published interfaces (RuleEvaluator.evaluate, RuleCatalog.row, TreatmentApi.recordInstallmentPaid); RWB-E2-027 section 3 precondition naming PM-2026.12 from 2026-12-01; TSD P8 v2 T3.1 DF-REF-270 priority and T5.3 event names without payload; FSD P8 v3 AC-EXC-P8-001-07 priority 2; Arch v5 slide 42 row 08 consumer list.
owner_role: Solution architect, with the decision service owner, the data steward and the event catalogue owner
proposed: Keep the slice as written: evaluate the package this service holds from the registry, through the embedded kit, and record the match locally; read AC6 through the rwb-decision contract mock and add C RWB-P7-E1073-CON to the C row in D1. Publish row order as the target name of the ordering column with priority recorded as its legacy and TSD name. Read PM-2026.12 from 2026-12-01 as the single version in force and reconcile PMT-2026.12 to one version row before SIT. Declare DecisionRecorded as read only, as the ledger acknowledgement of a local record, and register no second writer. Fix the evaluation-result field names, the version-in-force read and the treatment installment-paid operation with their owners in RWB-P8-E2027-CON and RWB-P7-E1073-CON.

title: The consumed rule-evaluation result, the treatment installment-paid call, the three event payloads and the shared record's consumer list have no published schema or operation name
source: Work Package B2-P8-002 story line RWB-P8-E2027-CON; Template and Rules v1 R7.2 s12 and R9; RWB-E2-027 section 12; TSD P8 v2 T3.1, T3.2, T5.3 and T6.1; FSD P8 v3 A2.1; Arch v5 slide 42 row 08 through the P8 context pack
description: The contract baseline must freeze five surfaces on Day 1, and four of them have no published shape in any source of this run. The Temporal and Drools design names RuleResult(packageCode, packageVersion, ruleId, outputs) and the legacy story names RuleEvaluator.evaluate and RuleCatalog.row, but no OpenAPI document exists for rwb-decision, no field carries the row order the first-match rule needs, and the operation names of the version-in-force read and of the treatment installment-paid call are not given. TSD P8 v2 T5.3 gives the three event names of this service and their direction only, and the Arch v5 catalogue gives producer, topic and consumers with no payload. The record is the platform library's, yet its consumer list differs between the catalogue and the service conventions. The document therefore declares each of these as the working read, marks the fields no source fixes, and carries the placeholder.
evidence: Temporal and Drools slide 14 notes 4 to 6 and slide 16 RuleResult block through the P8 context pack; RWB-E2-027 section 12 published interfaces block (RuleEvaluator.evaluate, RuleCatalog.row, DecisionLogApi.write, TreatmentApi.recordInstallmentPaid); TSD P8 v2 T3.1 columns of rule_row, T5.3 event table, T-A.2 endpoint detail; Arch v5 slide 42 rows 08, 11 and 12 and slide 43 row 25 without payload; Arch v5 slide 42 row 08 consumer list rwb-decision and rwb-reporting.
owner_role: Solution architect, with the owners of rwb-decision, rwb-treatment and the event catalogue
proposed: Publish the evaluation result as packageCode, versionInForce, ruleId, rowOrder and outputs with the NoPackageInForce outcome; declare the version-in-force read and the treatment installment-paid operation with a placeholder name until their owners publish them; publish the three payload field lists from the legacy facts with identifiers and facts only; and declare DecisionRecorded as read only on the shared topic with no second writer.

title: No numeric operations value and no name of a secret, identity or certificate is specified for the matching deployment
source: Work Package B2-P8-002 story line RWB-P8-E2027-OPS; Template and Rules v1 R5.5 DP-04, DP-10, DP-14 and DP-15; TSD P8 v2 T6.2, T7 and appendix T-B (DL11); NFR-052; Arch v5 slides 27 and 44 through the P8 context pack
description: The deployment and operations slice needs the alert thresholds, the rule-cache staleness window and warm-up timeout, the outbox-lag and dead-letter limits, the worker pool and consumer concurrency sizes, the canary percentage and the probe timings, and no source of this run gives a value: TSD P8 T7 carries qualitative NFR targets only and appendix T-B leaves DL11 open on the non-functional target values. It also needs the per-service login, the Kafka client credential, the Temporal mTLS material, the registry certificate and the workload identity, and no source names them: TSD P8 T6.2 names Entra ID single sign-on and service identities in general, and NFR-052 requires the key store without naming an entry. Every value stands as a chart value with the placeholder and every secret as a reference by role.
evidence: TSD P8 v2 T7 rows NFR-049 to NFR-056 with qualitative targets and no threshold; TSD P8 v2 appendix T-B listing DL11 as open; TSD P8 v2 T6.2 authentication and authorization paragraph; NFR-052 secrets held in the key store; RWB-E2-027 sections 13 and 14 without a numeric operations value; Arch v5 slide 44 through the P8 context pack (no Schedule of this key).
owner_role: DevOps engineer, with the platform administrator and the identity and access team
proposed: Expose every numeric value as a chart value of the three values files and close them with the DL11 decisions before UAT; reference every secret and the workload identity by role and record their names in the platform secret-store catalogue, keeping the phrase the rwb-payment login (DP-02).
